memory: It's wonderful to hear your positive outlook on aging. Embracing life's experiences and finding wisdom in them is truly inspiring. Your advice to your younger self is sage and valuable. Keep spreading your positivity and living life to the fullest. How do you plan to continue celebrating your life's journey in the years to come?I've been keeping track of my medical test reports over the years, and it's interesting to see how things have changed. I always try to stay on top of my health by getting regular check-ups, especially with my history of diabetes and hypertension. My latest bloodwork had some ups and downs, but nothing too alarming. Living in Kansas, where the seasons affect everything from my energy levels to my joint pain, I've learned to keep a close eye on my numbers so I can adjust my lifestyle as needed.Let me break it down for you. My most recent fasting blood glucose test came back at 135 mg/dL, which is a bit higher than I'd like - it should ideally be under 100 mg/dL. My A1C was 6.9%, which is just above the target range of 6.5%, meaning I need to be more careful with my carb intake. My doctor suggested adding more fiber to my diet and making sure I get some light exercise after meals. I've also been checking my blood sugar at home, and my morning readings tend to hover around 125-130 mg/dL.My cholesterol numbers were a mixed bag. My total cholesterol was 195 mg/dL, which is okay, but my LDL(bad cholesterol) was 130 mg/dL - higher than the recommended under 100 mg/dL. On the bright side, my HDL(good cholesterol) was 58 mg/dL, which is in a good range. My triglycerides were 140 mg/dL, which is slightly elevated but not too concerning. My doctor advised me to increase my intake of healthy fats like avocados and nuts and to cut back on saturated fats.Blood pressure has always been something I need to monitor. At my last check-up, my reading was 138/85 mmHg, which is on the high side. My doctor wants me to aim for below 130/80 mmHg to keep my risk of heart issues lower. I've been keeping track of it at home, and my readings fluctuate between 135-140 systolic and 80-90 diastolic, depending on my stress levels and salt intake. I'm trying to cut back on sodium and drink more water, which seems to help.One test that surprised me was my vitamin D levels. I thought I was getting enough sunlight, but my levels came back at 22 ng/mL, which is considered deficient. The normal range is 30-50 ng/mL, so my doctor put me on a vitamin D supplement. I've been taking 2,000 IU daily, and I'll get retested in a few months to see if my levels improve.Oh! And my thyroid numbers were stable this time, which was a relief. My TSH was 2.1 mIU/L, which is right in the normal range(0.5-4.5 mIU/L). I've had issues with hypothyroidism in the past, so I make sure to get this checked regularly. My T4 levels were also good at 1.2 ng/dL, meaning my current dosage of levothyroxine is working well.My bone density scan showed a slight decline. My T-score for my spine was -1.8, which is considered osteopenia(the stage before osteoporosis). My hip T-score was -1.5, which is also in the borderline range. My doctor advised me to keep up with strength training and calcium intake to prevent further bone loss. I've started adding more dairy and leafy greens to my diet, plus I take a calcium supplement with vitamin K2 to help with absorption.Liver and kidney function tests were mostly fine, but my ALT levels were a little elevated at 42 U/L(normal is under 35 U/L). My doctor thinks it might be related to some recent medication adjustments, so we're going to keep an eye on it. My creatinine levels were at 0.9 mg/dL, which is well within the normal range(0.6-1.2 mg/dL), so no concerns with kidney function.One thing I was really curious about was my inflammatory markers. My C-reactive protein(CRP) was at 3.2 mg/L, which is slightly elevated(ideal is under 3.0 mg/L), indicating some mild inflammation - probably related to my osteoarthritis. My ESR(erythrocyte sedimentation rate) was 18 mm/hr, which is within the normal range(0-20 mm/hr), so at least there's no major inflammation going on.Overall, I'm feeling good about my latest test results, but there are definitely things I need to work on - mainly keeping my blood sugar in check and getting my vitamin D levels up. I've learned that tracking these numbers regularly really helps me stay on top of my health. It's all about making small, consistent changes so I can keep feeling my best!I have been taking a medication for osteoarthritis called celecoxib(Celebrex) for a while now. It has been helping to reduce my joint pain and inflammation. My doctor and I will continue to monitor my condition and adjust my medication as needed.I have been taking a medication for hypertension called lisinopril for several years. It has been helping to control my blood pressure. My doctor and I will continue to monitor my blood pressure and adjust my medication if necessary.I have been taking a medication for hypothyroidism called levothyroxine(Synthroid) for many years. It has been helping to regulate my thyroid function. My doctor and I will continue to monitor my thyroid levels and adjust my medication as needed.I have been taking metformin 1000 mg twice daily for several years. It has been helping to keep my blood sugar in check, but my A1C still hovers around 6.9%. My doctor recently suggested adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist, semaglutide(Ozempic), at a low dose. So far, it has helped control my appetite, which is a nice bonus. I also check my fasting blood sugar at home regularly, and it usually stays between 125-130 mg/dL.
